rules.title: Match arms tested top-to-bottom, first matching arm runs
rules.statement: A `match` evaluates arms in source order; the first arm whose pattern matches (and whose guard, if any, holds) executes and the match completes. Operationally the arms form an if/else chain where each arm's test branches to the arm body on success and to the next arm's test on failure; an irrefutable pattern terminates the chain.

rules.title: Match guard evaluated after the arm's bindings are in scope
rules.statement: When an arm has a guard `if g`, the arm's pattern bindings are extracted and made visible to `g`; `g` is then evaluated as a boolean; if it holds the arm body runs (reusing the already-established bindings), otherwise control proceeds to the next arm. A failing guard does not fall through to other arms that share the same pattern test — the whole arm is skipped.

rules.title: Range pattern matches lo <= scrut <= hi inclusively
rules.statement: A range pattern `lo..=hi` matches a scrutinee value v iff `lo <= v && v <= hi` (both bounds inclusive). The comparison constants and the scrutinee are evaluated in the scrutinee's integer type.

rules.title: Range / scalar comparisons use unsigned ordering for unsigned scrutinees
rules.statement: For a scrutinee of unsigned integer type (u8/u16/u24/u32/u56/u64/u128), range-pattern bound comparisons use unsigned ordering (uge/ule); for signed scrutinees they use signed ordering (sge/sle).

rules.title: Or-pattern matches if any alternative matches
rules.statement: An or-pattern `a | b | ...` matches iff at least one alternative matches; alternatives are tested in order and the first match selects the arm. An alternative that is a wildcard or a bare binding (`_`, `n`) is irrefutable and matches unconditionally.

rules.title: `name @ subpat` binds the whole value and gates on subpat
rules.statement: An at-pattern `name @ subpat` binds `name` to the entire scrutinee value and matches iff `subpat` matches. The sub-pattern may be an or-pattern (matches if any alternative — int/bool/range — matches), a range (inclusive bounds, signedness per scrutinee), or a scalar pattern (int/bool/variant-discriminant equality).

rules.title: Scalar leaf patterns match by discriminant/value equality
rules.statement: A leaf pattern that reduces to a scalar discriminant — an int literal (its value), a bool (true=1/false=0), or an enum variant (its discriminant) — matches iff the scrutinee equals that discriminant, compared in the scrutinee's integer type.

rules.title: Refutable tuple pattern matches element-wise structurally
rules.statement: A non-empty tuple pattern matches iff every sub-pattern matches the corresponding tuple element. The tuple value is its inline by-value storage (a pointer to its fields); element sub-patterns are tested against the fields in place.

rules.title: Refutable struct pattern matches all named field sub-patterns
rules.statement: A struct pattern `S { f: p, ... }` matches iff every field sub-pattern `p` matches the corresponding field; refutable field sub-patterns are tested structurally against the struct's in-place field storage.

rules.title: Slice pattern on fixed-size array matches by element equality
rules.statement: A slice pattern over a fixed-size array `[T; N]` (or a `&[T; N]`/`&mut [T; N]`) matches iff each non-wildcard prefix and suffix scalar sub-pattern equals the array element at its index; wildcard sub-patterns impose no constraint; suffix indices are `N - suffix_count + k`. A reference to the array is the array base pointer (single indirection).

rules.title: Slice pattern on dynamic slice gates on runtime length
rules.statement: A slice pattern over a dynamic slice `&[T]` (fat pointer {data, len}) matches iff: with no rest `..`, `len == prefix_count + suffix_count`; with a rest, `len >= prefix_count + suffix_count`; plus each non-wildcard scalar prefix-element equals the corresponding runtime element.

rules.title: Reference pattern with scalar inner derefs then compares
rules.statement: Matching `&<scalar>` against a `&T`/`&mut T` scrutinee dereferences the reference (loads the pointee) and matches iff the loaded value equals the inner pattern's scalar discriminant.

rules.title: Leading `&` on enum pattern over deref'd tagged-enum scrutinee is peeled
rules.statement: When a `&Enum` scrutinee has been auto-deref'd to its tagged-enum form, an explicit reference pattern `&E::Variant{..}` / `&E::Variant(x)` / `&S{..}` has its redundant leading `&` removed so the inner variant/struct pattern is tested through the normal payload-extracting path (the no-payload C-like `&E::A` case keeps the dedicated reference handler).
rules.uncertainty: Auto-deref of &Enum to tagged form is established upstream in the same function; this unit only handles the resulting peel.

rules.title: let-else binds on match, else block must diverge
rules.statement: `let Pat = expr else { block };` tests `Pat` against `expr`: on match the pattern's bindings enter the enclosing scope and control falls through; on failure the else block runs and must diverge (terminate with return/unreachable). A named-wildcard pattern binds the value directly with no test; a unit variant tests the discriminant only; a data-carrying variant tests the discriminant and extracts payload bindings.
